title: I'm making an anti-grav racing game where you never touch the wheel
author: OCompany
selftext:
Hi all! I'm a solo dev building Neon Kamikaze GP in Godot 4: a racing management game set in a neon Tokyo.



You don't drive. You're the team boss. You give orders like CONSERVE, PUSH or KAMIKAZE, and your driver carries them out (mostly) at around 700 km/h.



In the clip, a part on my driver's car starts to fail mid-race. The race drops to quarter speed and asks one question: nurse it, run on, or retire?



What's in so far:

\- Every race is a full simulation, and it's seeded: the same calls give the same race. I replayed this one. Nursing the car got her home 5th. Saying nothing, the frame gave out on lap 31.

\- After the flag, a report tells you what ended your race, and whether a different plan might have saved it.

\- A six-team league. Rivals race by their own doctrines, and drivers age, improve, retire, and can be hurt or killed. The first driver to die in a sector gets a corner named after them.

\- A weekly parts market where your Engineer estimates every part for your car before you buy.



I use AI tools for the character art and backgrounds, and for much of the code.



No Steam page yet. I'm working toward a free Prologue.



A question for anyone who plays management sims: what makes watching a race you can't control feel tense rather than passive?
